review_description: Mark Group were very efficient only a few weeks from the time we spoke with their sales rep to installation. Unfortunately the same can't be said for our electricity supplier whom I had to chase up on several occasions over 2 - 3 months before we were up and running.

Mark Group Australia Pty Ltd installed the cable from the DC Isolator from the roof incorrectly, which caused a periodic error on the Inverter.Mark Group Australia Pty Ltd installed a dead data card in the Fronius inverter.Mark Group Australia Pty Ltd was very slow to repair their faults.I have hail damage on eight of the 39 solar panels; Renesola does not respond to my emails regarding a possible warranty claim for hail-damaged panels.Mark Group Australia Pty Ltd merged with Solgen.Renesola seems to have closed down in Australia.Avoid buying Renesola panels due to bad after-sales and warranty service.

Installed illegally, conduit tucked under tiles instead of sealed through a gasket. Dodgy wiring, wires crimped with pliers instead of proper crimped which were shorting. Brackets not trimmed.5 years of 50% production from a 5kw 9k system, little difference to bills & extremely poor customer service & follow up on repairs. STAY AWAY!!!!!

Our inverter (Fronius) has just started giving us an error code after 6yrs of service. We are no longer under warranty and so have had to go out and get quotes for a new inverter. Weâ€™ve now had two sparkies tell us that the Fronius inverter we have had installed by Mark Group looks to be a knock off version. And that the display does not accurately tell us what the issues is it even how much electricity we are putting back into the grid or even generating?

When we purchased the system we were given a 5 year Warranty on the inverter and 10 years o panels and installation but can not get anyone to fix the panels for us. We have been trying to get someone  for nearly tree months.
Lost hope in trying to contact this company. Once they have your money you no longer exist.

Sputnik manufactured inverter, they ceased operation.  Mark Group Australia sold inverter and installed inverter however, would not replace unit under warranty when it began to fault.  They said unit was still OK.  Mark Group Australia merged with SolGen Energy Australia who agreed it is covered by them now.  SolGen Energy will not even commit to inspect/repair/or replace inverter which has failed and no longer produces any power.  There is still 6 years warranty on the inverter.  A warranty seems to mean nothing when a company will not honor it, even though a warranty is promoted as a strong selling point.  There was no ranking for less than awful for customer service that I could choose.  The entire process has been an utter sham and awful experience.

This review comes after a very good experience at the installation five years ago before the Mark Group merged to become Solgen. Four weeks ago, the inverter packed it in. As I had taken out additional warranty, the unit was replaced. Delivered three days after initial phone contact in fact - thank you Amanda! However, trying to contact Solgen to arrange for an electrician to come out and install the new inverter has been impossible. Every time that I have rung - no matter the time of day - the main number is engaged ... the ubiquitous "Your call is important to us..." for as long as it takes to get the shits and hang up. The one direct line that I have goes to voicemail and no return call. The email address I have elicits no response either and the "Contact Us" on the Solgen web page, gets no response either.  All of which makes me think this is in receivership or closed its doors.

Finn, I know this feedback comes years after the asking - apologies for this, lost email file - but first point is the survey needs rethinking. Even after 5 years in service I have no real way to evaluate value for money, quality of system, installation or customer service because I have no basis for comparison. I've selected "good" for each category but all this means is "good enough that I haven't wanted to have it removed for any reason". The system works but I have no way of knowing if it is any better or worse than any other system supposedly offering similar performance.On the plus side it has paid for itself (just) over the 5 years we've had it, but only because we get a good feed-in rate. On the down side, performance has declined >3% per year which is a bit more than I expected. Now with some experience in this, if I were thinking of doing it all again with today's options, I'd install double the capacity - more if possible - using east & west facing roof faces, not just north, and look hard at batteries. Would also want a way to isolate from the grid during transmission failures, i.e. don't necessarily want to go off grid, but don't want grid problems to prevent access to solar or battery power while grid is being repaired. With current setup, the solar system is useless if the grid is down.FYI, panels are Trina Honey (x16) and I'd look hard at higher end panels with more output and longer performance life.

Purchased 4,75kw system in 2014. Mark Group didn't tell me about the government rebate. When i contacted them a few months after purchase they told me that the rebate had come off the initial purchase price. They got a contractor to install the system. The people did a poor job of installing and damaged my colorbond roof putting creases in it by not walking on the rafters and then tried to say they were already there. Which i know they weren't, as i helped put the roof on.

I was concerned that we were not getting our moneys worth from a very expensive system. Our electricity retailer said we should phone back the supplier Mark Group.  On sending them the figures straight off the Inverter Panel we now find that the feed in is far less than it should be meaning we are not feeding back what we should, nor are we really being energy wise by using electrical appliances.......while we are producing bugger all solar electric. Part of the problem was that there was no follow up from the group and remembering the Home Insulation Fiasco I should have followed up myself.  But at some stage you need to take things in good faith.  Never again and never, ever with these guys whatever they call themselves.

Put solar on in 2012 first inverter went in 2014 had it replaced now it has failed. Now they tell me warranty starts from first inverter not the replacement so that's 2 inverters in under 6 years don't go near this company I think this is a ripoff if they cannot warrant the replacement. Rang them all you get is call centre they don't give a dam just want to take next call. Stay away

The Mark Group refuse to acknowledge our 10 year warranty. We bought it with an extended 5 year warranty on top of the existing 5 year limited warranty. They claim it is not showing on their system as having the extended warranty. We have it on our paperwork so we may have to go to Fair Trading. We are very disappointed with the Mark Group. These companies need to take responsibility for what their sales people promise and sell. I hope we can sort this out soon as it is very stressful.

Since being installed in 2015 our bill has gone up, we have paid $6118.78 in elec bills since solar installed, have had a total buy back of $34.20.The day they put panels up the meter was suppose to go in but the guys here said they weren't putting meter in today, my husband said that's why l took the day off so l could have trench ready to lay leads, and cover up so they put meter in, now our bill is higher than it ever was, and the Solgen person looking after my case winged about having 172 other cases she was working on and her CEO has given her some of his cases, and she would get to it as soon as possible, finally a week ago an electrician came, he had never seen the type of meter we have, and Solgen said he has still not put his report in, so we pay while we wait. They don't return calls, there is no after sales service, we have complained since day 1 about outer solar and were told it was us, using more than we were making, but we weren't making anything, if anyone has any suggestions l am open to hear them, we just wanted a cheaper electricity bill and it has gone up and we have to pay for the solar system as well.

Two of the ten panels were place in a situation where windows reflected onto them under some sun conditions.  This caused a marked reduction in output from the panels.  Mark Group were contacted several times and were always happy to talk but not to act.  An electrician finally came out and claimed the problem was caused by dust (the panels had been washed 3 weeks prior).  I finally fixed the problem by moving these panels to a different place on the roof.

Installers broke tiles which went undetected until we had heavy rain. So much water into ceiling cavity and then through the ceiling that I had a waterfall in my bedroom. Mark Group eventually returned and replaced roof tiles but no attempt to even look at internal damage. My ski gear, my wedding dress, my kids' baby momentoes, all sodden with filthy water from the roof. Not to mention the ceiling, carpet etc. In addition I can see very little savings on my power bill despite getting the panels with highest efficiency.

Installed today - June 10, so all still very new! However everyone associated with Mark Group from Michael in sales to Harry and his installation team - they were all very helpful and very professional! Let's hope it delivers everything as promised!!
Inverter blew up after 4 years.Promised by Solgen to fix within a week, THREE MONTHS later still awaiting the fix.

Thanks to Finn I've been able to get: a small system I could afford on the pension; with a good company whom I trust; and a local sales person who was great and sincere; and an installer who is also local and professional.

For after installation service this company is the PITS!!!!   We were very happy dealing with them, THE MARK GROUP, at the start but once you have a problem BE PREPARED - no return phone calls EVER! and this has been going on since July and it is now end of November. They have told us several times a new panel is on its way. We have lots of emails on that, most unanswered by them, asking for delivery details. It still hasn't been sent. They keep saying yes they will post it, and it never is. They don't return calls,EVER!!!!! We have dealt with three separate persons, two no longer working there but still no better service with our new contact. We are preparing to seek legal advice as to the next step we can take.

We bought our system 2 years ago at a cost of $9,000. The most we have saved in a quarter is $75 most of the time it has been $20 a quarter. I know the Marks Group company is under new management as I had previously lodged a complaint and I did receive a phone call advising me that the company was under new management so the new management is aware that the system has never worked. I thought that during the day the electrical  appliances would run on solar on a clear day ( and we have plenty f those in Cairns) however our power bill remained as high as it had always been before we had the solar installed. All I really wanted was to cut my power costs down so I installed a heat pump hot water system and my electricity bill has halved. I really didn't need to install a useless solar system that is never going to pay for itself in my lifetime and the idiot sale rep should have told me that instead of ripping us off with all of the crap about how much money we will save and how the system will pay for itself. When we received our first electricity bill after having the solar installed I called the sales rep and complained that we had only saved $20 and his response was that the weather had been exceptionally hot so the fridges were working overtime and I should try putting tubs of ice in the fridge to help keep them cool.

Mark Group were the only one who sent a person to see us and our property, the others just emailed quotes.The sales advisor was very knowledgeable and provided us with a great deal of sound information about how to get the best from a solar installation. He recognised the unique nature of our property and came up with several alternatives i.e. different panels & inverters.As we wished to have minimum panels and maximum efficiency we chose Sunpower 327w panels & Fronius Inverter which seem to be leaders in the field.

The sales pitch was great but from there poor response time, much less output than promised, missing roof tiles (explained by Solvent as probably stolen!!??), shaded up tiles not fixed including under the panels, blocked valleys to the point our ceiling flooded and crashed to the floor, paperwork signed off by unverified installer and under a possible false name, the switch burst into flames, no responsibility taken by the company, lying and blaming others. They have caused untold misery and cost 10s of 1000s of dollars. I strongly advise staying away from them.

Installation of system including panels and inverter completed on 3rd December 2015.Inverter at installation date found not to function. Required service technician to establish cause of problem.Had to wait till  Saturday 12th Dec for service check.  Took some time to establish fault.Fault apparently due to grid voltage being high at 256 volt rather than required voltage at 240 volts.Inverter does not function at the higher voltage. Need to upgrade inverter to Queensland standard which operates at higher voltage.Could not access inverter code to make necessary changes to inverter . Hopefully will obtain code from Fronius onMonday 14th Dec. If so not sure when technician will be able to make changes to inverter.Indicated that it will not happen before Christmas and may have to wait till middle of January 2016.Very disappointed with this service approach as system has been fully paid for.

After being promptly provided with quotes I contracted Mark Group. I believe work was of good quality but customer service was lacking. A Solar Analytics was included by the salesman. When the main solar panel system was installed in October I kept pursuing the salesman for the Solar Analytics. I finally gave up, called Mark Group to find the salesman no longer worked there, no-one had informed me, and that I needed a new switch board (no-one had told me that either) before the Analytics could be installed. This was just before Christmas and I couldn't find an installer until late January to replace the switchboard. Then I kept chasing Mark Group for the Solar Analytics to go in. This took 6 more weeks of phone calls and promises.Finally, from getting quotes in September, we are finally up and running mid-March. The system appears to be performing well.

It has been 3 weeks since instillation and the system is not working yet!!! apparently due to and Energex high voltage issue. So I have selected "average" above until the system is operational (hopefully before my next power bill!!!!). When it is operational I will do this survey again and hopefully my remarks will be better.

I find it hard to rate the solar system yet. I would be more qualified to review it after I have seen a couple of electricity bills.Also I am a bit confused with a notice from ERGON with fault defects and they haven't put their reader in yet. My electrician seems to think the electrician who installed the system should have to rectify the faults and bring the meter box up to ERGON standards.

Originally Mark Group did not quote.  They had an issue with their sales rep and the quote was delayed 6 weeks.  I was quite annoyed at the delay.The Mark Group have since supplied the best value for money and cheapest quote alternative.  We have actually sized a 15kw battery ready system with 19kW of solar panels, (3 phase).  They have not installed yet as we are waiting on Energex approvals.The system also has 10 year warranties on the equipment and the installation.

Whilst there was nothing wrong with the service from Ionic we decided on the Mark Group due solely on the professionalism.In fact the Mark Group was slightly more expensive with their salesman more experienced and explaining things in more detail.This was probably the only difference The installers were really good - working all day in light rain.Thank you for your help in this - we only got connected to the grid about ten days ago so will need to be a bit patient for end of September.Thanks again.David

Still waiting for Energex to install the new meters. Everything else rates very highly but Energex very poorly.We were particularly happy with our Mark Group rep who enlightened us greatly whereas both other reps simply wanted to sell us the biggest system they could.
Currently in the process of having my system installed so too early to provide a full picture of my experience
Polite and helpful salesperson. No fuss installation. so far no problems but too soon to comment on much else. Clyde
All went fast and smooth and from wo to go we were up and running in less than a month

I was impressed with the salesman's knowledge and how he explained it all worked.  Some information I knew and some I didn't. Generally I thought it was all a good deal.  They were slightly more expensive than others, and I even looked at ones not suggested by Finn Peacock, but the price difference was only marginal.  I investigated the systems offered by doing my own research and what the Mark Group offered was reasonably top of the line for what I could pay and so worked in well with my allotted budget. The workman came and installed it rather quickly and the workmanship was good. All people I spoke to were professional and courteous and one thing I require when making a substantial purchase is that the seller respects that money is hard to come by and that spending such a large amount (by my standards!) can be fraught with worry if I'm doing the right thing or going with the right company.  All in all, I was pleased with the service and felt comfortable that I went with the right company.  Thank You to Finn Peacock for making this site up as I was struggling a little with the idea of purchasing solar but his assistance made it so much easier.

A very complex investigation is required  - from prices , solar panel types , inverter models etc.This took me 3 months of solid dedication to come to an informed decision - I have become some what of a solar expert ??I would not recommend buying through a cheap solar company - evidence has shown me that U really do get what U pay for with solar systems.
BrightEarth electrical were contracted for the installation. They were super professional and very efficient. We're also happy to discuss and respond appropriately to all of my queries.
Ergon Energy Mucked us about with approval for the Install for over 4 weeksNot installers fault, they installed as soon as approval granted.

Installer very knowledgeableFollow-up conversations with Head Office lack knowledge of their product & information on Meter Readings. No one in their office is able to answer questions about the running of the Solar (how much power needed to run dishwasher etc)In & working in 3 weeks, we made 15 calls to Electric Co. and SupplierSo far, we are happy. Thanks for your help

Mark Group contractor was very professional with the install. The other two companies I received quotes from were also very professional and in the end it was a comment from Finn regarding the performance of one of the panels available which helped my decision to choose Mark Group. Unfortunately it must be close to five weeks and I am still waiting for Origin to install the digital meter in order for the proper use of the solar system.  The companies suggested by Finn were top tier contractors. Thanks Finn.

Was given incorrect / incomplete information about availability and cost of "off peak" electricity to my propertyInstalled 16/3/16 no grid connection until 26/5/16 - not happy about thatHead Office / salesman / installer have all failed to respond to email questions posed by me at different timesOn occasions when I have rung Head Office, you are not even put in a queue if no one is available.

The salesperson was very helpful and was able to answer all our questions - even hard ones!  The installation was difficult because of the way our power is set up (rural property) and that resulted in the installation not being as smooth as it should have been.  The admin staff were helpful but a bit slack getting back to us or fixing up the problems which cropped up.  However eventually most things were ironed out - just took a lot longer than it should. We look forward to seeing the difference on the power bill.  We were told more than once that we'd made the right choice with our supplier and it certainly was better than one of the other suppliers quotes who thought that we would be happy with a 3.8kW system (for the same price) when we'd asked for a 6kW one!
I purchased 2 systems of about equal value. 1 at me house Townsville and one for my daughter at the farm Eltham NSW. This one has not yet been completed.
A bit of messing around with the EWR form due to phase mismatch between Supply and Metering.

Had some difficulty receiving the paperwork weeks after paying. The accounts person wanted payment the day of installation. We explained we will pay the next day but he tried to get us to pay by credit card ( even though he knew there will be a 1.9% surcharge ).

We did experience some electrical issues when the installers put the system in as our home security system and the electrical circuit in my shed was somehow shorted out on the day of the install. No resolution yet other than installer saying we should have turned off any delicate elec appliances when we contacted them about the issues.We then had security company come and look into the fault and they said it was something the installers did, but neither party are willing to accept responsibility.
It was a great negotiation with the company

The sales person was well spoken and not pushy. Most importantly he treated my 7 year old son in the same way he treated me and my wife, answering every one of his child minded questions without hesitation or sarcasm and answering them as if I had asked them myself.

It has taken me 4 months from first contacting them and accepting the finished job.I accepted their quotation on 10/09/14, and paid the required deposit.Time went on so I rang them to find out what was going on, and I was advised there was a backlog of Canadian panels, and they were waiting a shipment.Finally the panels arrived and were installed on 18/12/14, and I finalised payment with the expectation of being up and running within the advised maximum 2 week period. However Christmas and New Year came which possibly slowed things down again.But I can now advise as from today 20/01/14, the system is up and running.I can honestly say the workmanship was up to scratch, and it could have been the result of me letting it slip I held an Electrical Supervisor Ticket, and had worked in the renewable sector for approx. 35 years, both Hydro and Wind.

My Experience with all parties concerned with solar installation was excellent with the exception of Ergon. They made my installation zero export and I feel that if I buy from them what they provide then they should buy from me what I provide. Being a pensioner I saw export as a saving for me, which would help offset some of the prices rises elsewhere which we have to cope with.

The first question is misleading. I picked Mark Group firstly because they had good reviews on your website but also from personal recommendations from a person who had done a huge amount of research and gone with them. Yes, they were considerably more expensive, but I believe the quality of the panels and inverters I had installed more than compensates for that. I told each supplier that my decision would be based on the quality of their system, not on their price or other gimmicks.

The salesperson explained the system to me in terms I could understand and answered any questions I had. Mark Group also offered a special deal with Diamond Energy that I will follow up once I am connected to the grid.

Great........Average..........Poor!!Sales was great, very helpful and ready to answer your concerns.Once they have your business its a series of emails explaining the process, but no personal touch to guide you, just another customer in line.My install was not great. First, they scheduled me in the afternoon for a double story house - expecting me to let the installer intrude on my evening.I also requested that conduits from one level to another be placed to one side of the wall, so its not easily seen. but that was ignored and it was placed right in the middle where is was obvious.I dealt with the installer directly (after the install manager forwarded my complaint to them) it will cost me an extra $200 to get the conduit re-route.Advise: don't pay in full up-front and talk to the installer before they proceed with work. AND CONSIDER ANOTHER COMPANY.

If you are looking at purchasing a solar system, please also take into consideration after sales service of the supplier.  It has been over 1 month since my inverter died, I have  called Mark Group and left message after message for someone to contact me regarding this matter.  No one has bothered to return my calls.  I contacted SolarMax in Germany and got a response within a few hours. Turns out my inverted needs to be replaced.  No wonder Mark Group wont return my calls, it appears they don't want to honour the warranty.  I'm $10,000 out of pocket, needless to say my experience has not been a good one.  Please, before you commit to anything, research everything.
Seems they are too busy to handle my quires and follow up the installation faults (early December). Anyway, everything has been fixed and the solar syatem works very well.

Filling out the Solar Quotes survey was very helpful.  Having a couple of companies contact us gave us information to compare and work with. We could do some homework.We found Paul Jacox from Mark Group a friendly and professional salesman.  He wasn't pushy at all, explained the details of the system and its suitability to us well,  and was happy to come to our remote location to consult and ultimately get a good deal for us.The installers were efficient, professional  and worked hard in appalling heat the day they installed the system.Now we just have to wait for the energy company to connect us.  That wont be until early January which will be 6 weeks since instalment.So far we don't know how effectively the system works but have high hopes for its suitability and long term economical and environmental benefit.
Mark Group seemed a bit thin on staff in Victoria and a little hard to contact locally and there was bit of glitch in scheduling the CEC

The initial approval from S.A. Power came through very quickly but, due to a change of Inverter, a new approval was needed. This is yet to come so, six weeks after installation we are no closer to being grid connected. I'm not sure whose fault this is .

The installer was very professional and did a great job,except.  The job started with the installer moving things on the roof to clear space for the panels, moving whirlybirds then measured the available space.  He then consulted with me on the configuration.  He came up with a better way to place the panels.  The design engineer used Google earth or similar for the design and it just didn't work and needed more hardware than was needed, extra cost.  Then it came to the inverter.  The installer had no idea what to do with the data card that was supplied with the inverter.  He was on the phone for 30min and when I asked how it was going, he informed me that it was good and the data card was installed.  The job was completed with him showing me all the safety requirements.Now the problems started.  I asked the Mark Group, how does the monitoring work?  I was instructed to go to a website and download things, watch videos and do as they say.  WHAT, I have to do this?  Turns out that the inverter uses WiFi for the monitoring.  OK, I can do that.  After several frustrating hours, I got nowhere.  Again got on to the Mark Group and finally the Senior Design Engineer got back to to try and solve it.  90 min on the phone later we got nowhere.  Turns out the WiFi is only good for 10 metres and won't work through a brick wall.  A week later, my two sons spent 6 hrs to get the monitoring complete over a LAN cable.  The Mark Group and the installer had no idea how to do this.  Thanks to my sons Chris and Josh it is now working.  Great system, just lacks installation knowledge.
it didnt take as long as i thought it would  everything was ahead of the projected timetable well done

A bit disappointed with the output due to my North West oriented house. The best I get is 2.5 kW out of the 4kW system. Because I am using micro inverters I am going to try orienting one panel to North facing with 27 degree tilt. If thereâ€™s a substantial improvement Iâ€™ll consider re-orienting the rest
Very professional. Turned up on time & completed the work in good time without any damage & removed all waste materials on completion.

The salesperson was extremely knowledgeable, helpful and friendly. I had completed considerable research and the information he supplied confirmed what I had discovered. There were no outrageous claims of efficiency etc. Very happy with the job and the Company.
Mark Group were professional and helpful with all facets of the process. Sales staff were competent and knowledgeable.
The system hasnt been installed as yet due to building delays. I have paid a deposit.

I totally recommend Mark Group, the sales guy (Ian) was very honest & helped us to decide what's best for our needs & didn't push for a larger unit which would have been a waste of money. If we wanted, we can upgrade if our power needs change in the future. I was blown away that I didn't need to organise anything, Mark Group did all the ground work. Also the electrical installers they contracted are very professional.

I believe I have gotten the best quality system i could afford, but I felt that Mark Group is mostly about sales pitch. Once they had my money (before the system was installed), it felt like that was their job done.The people who installed the system were not Mark Group employees (they were very nice and installed the system very quickly despite the weather, but they also trampled my poor garden to death) and only came back to explain the system to me when I asked.
I was happy that we could pay it off

Fantastic Installation and Customer Service.  Sent them a couple of emails about my concerns with the proposed locations of the panels; and my inverter got upgraded to suit two strings of panels!  System has already produced more than 315kw since it was turned on a couple of weeks ago.  On really good days I get Zero, Zilch, No, Nada, consumption from the grid from 10am till 6pm this summertime; and more than half of the energy produced is sent to the grid.  Its a pity that my smart meter has not been recalibrated by Powercor to this day so I don't get any FITs for the time being.Definitely will recommend!  Job very well done.
Simple process thanks to the quotes and your service Finn. Would have been  much more complicated process.

Not enough info given at install - no written info left and I was unclear as to process with Ergon. Took six weeks before system was connected, but money already collected for system...uinimpressed.Follow up regarding availabiltiy of battery has been non-existent. Company estimated battery to be available by Dec 2014 and would contact me. Sept 2015 and i have heard nothing.

Positives: Overall, very happy with the unit and the quality of the installation. Also, they were very accomodaing in installing a WATTSON solar monitor at my request. Happy they are replacing broken tiles. Finally, very happy with the overall level of customer service offerred (most people I spoke to in the Mark Group were quite willing to spend time on the phone working through issues).Challenges: Information does not flow fell internally - work on the assumption that every person you speak to doesn't know what your requirements are. Example 1, agreed design for positioning of panels was ignored by installers and initially put in the wrong place - this was 'fixed' at the time but isn't quite where we wanted - hence the 'average' for installation. Example 2 - request to be notified prior to installation of the new meter (so I could be there) wasn't followed through.Overall - the unit is working well, most of the people were really helpful - their challenges seem to be around a 'small company' becoming a 'big company' and having gaps.
They were well organised, helpful and responsive
Company in Australia not very well co-ordinated.They appear very well organised at first, however I have become concerned about some of their practices!!  Time will tell. Products appear 1st rate.
It's hard to rate our supplier at the stage. Only time will tell if its been "value for money" and a "Quality System"

I got two other quotes but they were a bit pricey for a 4kw. An installer really needed to come out and have a close look at the roof  When they got here the battens were too far apart and they had to change their plans which the designer had drawn up in Sydney using Nearmap.
Mark Group was excellent.Installer took one week to complete job

Initial sales and system information, installation and performance of the system had been good experiences. The follow-up service from The Mark Group has been appallingly bad. The wrong inverter was installed and while The Mark Group admitted their error they have done nothing about it. Over the space of several months and numerous calls to the company nothing has happened. Despite promises that I will have calls returned or that I will be informed of what is happening - absolutely nothing. The sales information that supposedly sets this company apart from others is that its after sales service is exemplary and unlike other 'here today gone tomorrow' companies in the solar energy installation field they will support their customers. I cannot agree with their claims. I have estimated the cost to them for the inverter upgrade (to what was contracted to be installed) is a mere $250.00. This is a chickenfeed a amount of money and pales in comparison to the amount of goodwill lost by such poor customer service. I also intend to lodge a formal Consumer Affairs complaint because the system installed is not what it was contracted to be.

We had a few questions a few weeks after the install. I called mark who was the first contact from our solar provider and he has been the GREATEST help even getting someone from our energy provider to come help us with a few things.I have been recommending him and the mark group to every one I know wanting solar.So very impressed.

After placing the order dealing with the Mark Group was quite difficult - they are a large company managing our project from their Melbourne office, and it was very difficult to find out at what stage our project was and who was handling it, also asking questions about the design, documentation, quality and compliance of their system and components. The end result was satisfactory but they were not good at keeping the customer informed after placing the order.
Mark Australia was the only company to contact me have bought 2 4kw systems as we are building a duplex. Installation should be in about 6 months

The sales rep was very friendly new what he was talking about. He was upfront and answered all my questions. The installation was very quick and professional, the guys came at about 7:30 am and were done by 10:30 am. They explained the system afterwards. I am very happy with the process so far.

Paid $10,000 for 7KW with Fronius 3 phase inverter with WiFi and Renesola panels. Also Mark Group installers were not contractors.Had an issue with one of the panel mounts just after installation but couldn't get anyone to call back. Fixed it myself.All salespeople had no clue about the technical stuff, but Mark Group  salesperson would let me talk to their technical gurus.I shudder to think what customers get if they just ring a salesperson and go with the cheapest price. There is no doubt that solar power is the way to go.  It is worthwhile spending time getting your head around exactly what to look for.  I found SolarQuotes extremely helpful in this regard.  In simple terms you need to go with a reputable company [read reviews and pay little attention to the salesperson who comes to your door].  You need to invest in quality panels.  You will not make money from solar,  only save it so get a system that is in line with your average daily consumption.  Go for a quality inverter.  Ensure all components of your system have a written warranty that is covered by a company with a strong Australian presence.  Installation is important and you are really in the hands of the contractors used by the solar company.  Again read reviews.  Get at least 3 quotes and remember that your rebate goes to the solar company. [so a 7k quote is really approx. a 10k quote].  There is considerable markup so be prepared to negotiate.  I have dealt with a company [Modern solar - based in Tullamarine Melbourne.].  The salesman was a shifty individual who espoused that the panels, inverter and installation were the best quality around.  There were no 3rd party reviews in existence.  The original price of 21k for a 5k system was meant to shock [it did].  Then a charade between the salesman and his boss on the end of the phone [3 calls] brought the price down to 11,900 if you allowed them to advertise on you property and keep this special price confidential.  Some Coles vouchers were also promised.  Had to lodge a VCAT application to get a deposit returned after 5 months.  Lesson here is to do all of your research before paying a deposit because if you call the company to come to you they are not bound to honour the statutory 10 day cooling off period.  So they claim but it can still be decided by a Tribunal and it can depend on the cost of work undertaken before you cancel the installation.  Tip of the day..If you hear about a Black Crow fly the other way.

One key element that the Mark Group sales person reiterated a number of times is that Mark Group do not use external contractors as this allows them to maintain a high level of quality on installs. Very happy with the installation team and the sales rep. Gave a good explanation of the systems and the features. The staff at the office were also very helpful. We opted for an interest free payment option through GE money, did have some difficulty getting paper work from them to show the terms of the loan agreement. It was eventually sorted and the repayments are less that the cost of our old electricity bill minus the savings. So we consider this an affordable option.  The other point is when you switch to solar your contract will change with your supplier. We are with Energy Australia and paid 27.885 c/kWh before solar, the new plan is for peak and off peak the chargers are 37.103 c/kWh for peak and 17.765 c/kWh for off peak with a 8.8 c/kWh buy back these cost include GST. We also receive a 10% discount if we pay on time. I called around and found some better deals. Origin quoted 34.35 c/kWh for peak and 16.82 c/kWh for off peak with a 8.8 c/kWh buy back. They also offered a 22% discount if you pay on time. So it pays to shop around. Looking at making a change to my supplier or seeing if Energy Aust will match Origin. Just a note that off peak is from 11pm to 7am and all weekend.

I sought* a 3kW system to comfortably exceed my forseeable demands but with a limited amount of shade free roof:* which encouraged me to go for high efficiency panels (SunPower),* the panels on tilt frames to face approximately north at 25deg elevation and bring the output peakearlier in the day for clothes washing, daytime cooking and vacuum cleaning etc.* the panels to be mounted in "landscape" orientation for reduced wind loads and visual impact.This took some negotiation, even partway through the  installation day, due to mis-communication between the Mark Group designer and the installation team. I feel that the modern approach of communicating drawings and specifications via a small-screen mobile phone was most unsatisfactory and initially ignored by the installer. I had to show him the agreed design on a larger PC screen. The installation was subsequently reworked satisfactorily though with one redundant roof penetration for me to patch.Although I felt the installation team took electrical safety very conscientiously, I was not comfortable with their casual approach to moving around the roof carrying heavy components with scant regard to bending the roofing steel, on a roof sloping to a 5m drop onto concrete. Despite my reservations, no workers or PV panels fell off and the roof remains undinted.Part of the specification I should have pursued in more detail was data readout from the inverter. To characterise seasonal, site and weather factors in matching our load scheduling, I made it clear I wanted a means of logging time-of-day output. The iverter documentation appeared to promise this but on familiarisation with the software after installation, I discovered it does no such thing. Only day, month and yearly aggregates are stored and only by manual intervention. I am left with the task of exploring alternative software which is proving far from straight forward.

Then the installers told me the system did not have bypass diodes - despite the fact I had expressly asked and had the salesman confirm that bypass diodes were infact part of the system. In the end, we had to settle for a 2.5kW system and I had to chase the company and ultimately speak to the State Service manager who finally confirmed that bypass diodes were indeed part of the system... But he also advised that my understanding of how bypass diodes work (as garnered from this website) was incorrect. They don't "bypass" significantly shaded panels to prevent the system from dropping in power production across the board. They are more designed to bypass "failed" cells within panels (ie more a safety measure than one designed to mitigate the impacts of shading). Nonetheless, after much discussion and follow up, I am ultimately convinced that the system we have paid for and had installed is indeed of a very high quality and it will still deliver us significant power/cost savings. Still no call back!!I must state that I had paid in full and was feeling that I was being given the brush off by now. I called again and the lady told me that the connection would be in about a week.Anyway, a couple of days passed and I received a call saying that Energy Australia had flagged my system with a new legislation where by if you had a 5 kW system or greater then connection to the grid would have to be with 3 phase and not single phase which is all my house has! I was fuming by now and I went to the office to speak with them, I was thinking that they should have known this.Apparently, this law was brought out in 2012 and nobody was working to it, the engineer told me there was a cooling of period before the law was in! They new of this law but still put a 5 kW system on my house were there is no 3 phase connection! Anyway, their solution was to replace my 3 kW inverter with a 2.8 kW inverter and then I would have a 4.8 kW system and connection could go ahead. They gave me a $200 refund for the reduction and my connection is planned for next week. They told me there would be no noticeable difference from the 5 kW system to a 4.8 kW system, it works out to be about 67 kW difference a year! Fingers crossed I will be switched on next week. I think that Solar Australia need to have a few lessons in customer skills, but the installation team were really very professional. Probably because they were contractors.

Mark Group sales person presented  himself and hence, followed up through out until installation was completed. He explained everything in full details.True Value rang me but never showed up and was pushy over the phone.Green Engineering showed up but offered poor quality products.

I can not recommend The Mark Group strongly enough to anyone who is looking at getting a solar PV system installed. Two of the three invited companies did not initially respond. The Mark Group was one of those two. They needed nudging to give a quote. Installation was quick and efficient. Nice bunch of blokes who got on with the job; very professional.Before and after sales service was top notch also. The sales person gave me the facts and supported my decision to get a 2 kW system instead of the 5 kW system I was originally going to get. Saving me a few thousand dollars.
This company is a world respected installer, very happy with final lay-up & overwhelming power produced per day..Trina Honey PVs.

They turned up when they said they would, there was no pressure, they answered all of my questions.Installation, the same as above and they cleaned up after themselves and also showed me how the system worked and what to do if there was a fault.I would use this company again, they were great!

I am really annoyed that although I have paid for the system it is still not hooked up to the grid. They blame essential energy and vice versa. I think that should be all sorted before installation so that it does what it is reported to do!! Very poor!!

The sales rep from Mark Group, Phil, was the nicest of the 3 and was the only one who didn't seem to be in a hurry to get in and get out. We have found all the staff at the Mark Group that we have dealt with to be highly professional, always willing to answer any question that we may have and we would have no hesitation in recommending the Mark Group to our friends.However we were a bit disappointed when the they came to install the panels they were unable to fit enough panels for 5kW system  on the available roof space even though two other representives from the Mark Group had done measurements and both had said it would be okay and as a result we could only have a 4.45KW system and of course the bank cheque was the wrong amount and had to be cancelled, however the Mark Group have agreed to reimburse us for the cost of the cancelled cheque.

Mark group were the only ones who offered an alternative panel than the standard mono. They took our circumstances into account when settling the final price. The sales man Shaun was very knowledgeable and answered every question we had plus some.

They were not the cheapest, but were still competitive. Their representative, Cliff Bowles came to the house and answered all our questions and was very personable. The installation occurred quickly and the connection to the grid only a few days later. Installers came within a week of signing the contract, arrived on time, did extra work in fixing a number of cracked tiles at no extra cost.   Were very informative, made no mess and even though it was a big job (20 Panels in 4 locations) were finished in the day.

Very happy with the service from the organisation. The installation team were fantastic with no problems. The paperwork was completed by company efficiently and have had no issues to deal with. Still waiting to see the benefits on our power bill but looks as if our bills will be virtually nothing.

Very pleased with The Mark Group and the whole experience. Good advice. Good system. Good value. I am glad I went through Solar Quotes. Saved me a whole lot of time by pre-screening potential providers.

I would recommend The Mark Group to anyone who wishes to install solar power. Salesman appeared knowledgeable and installation was quick, however that was when the problems began.  We purchased 20x250W CanadianSolar panels and a 5kW SMA inverter, one of 3 standard systems Mark Group offer.  Checking the installation against the inverter manual revealed the installation exceeded the design limits of the SMA inverter such that on good production days the inverter would shut down.  Contacting Mark Group turned up a massive design error where the entire output of the panels was put onto one input on the SMA, exceeding the maximum input current by 20%.  Many phone calls and several return visits by the installers over the past month and we are still without a working system.  Leaves us wondering how many other installations have used this design and have the same problem.  Overall opinion of Mark Group:- communication - poor, documentation - very poor, customer service - very poor, knowledge of installers - very poor, willingness to fully resolve issues - poor.  Would not recommend Mark Group to anyone.
